title: E0 baseline-integrity checkpoint form B
instructions: Protect the validity and interpretation of a first objective baseline. Complete both decisions before submitting.

parts.prompt: A power cut closes a learner's saved baseline halfway through. Which recovery best preserves one traceable attempt?

options.text: Read all answer explanations before restarting
Create several new attempts and keep the highest score
Ask classmates about the unfinished questions
Resume the saved attempt, record the interruption and avoid discussing unseen items

choice_rationales.B: Repeated exposure turns the baseline into coached practice.
choice_rationales.D: Saved-state recovery plus an interruption note preserves continuity and transparency.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A technical interruption should be documented while the original independent attempt is resumed.

parts.prompt: After several weeks of learning, which comparison best tests improvement while reducing answer-memory effects?

options.text: Repeat the identical form with correct answers highlighted
Compare only the questions previously answered correctly
Use a secure matched form covering the same blueprint with fresh prompts
Replace the test with a confidence rating

choice_rationales.A: Answer recall would dominate the result.
choice_rationales.B: Removing weak areas changes the blueprint.
choice_rationales.C: A matched fresh form preserves comparability while testing transfer.
choice_rationales.D: Self-report is different evidence from objective performance.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: A parallel form measures the same constructs using unseen material, reducing simple recall.
